notes: A re-review of G4a-2b. The fix was a server change, so pass 1 stopped to ask the user; they chose to fix the server in this review. The first commit attempt was refused by the pre-commit golangci-lint with five SA5011 reports in pending_deletion_targeting_test.go, a file this change does not touch; a clean HEAD worktree linted with 0 issues and so did the tree after 'golangci-lint cache clean', so the reports came from a stale local cache. Voice messages still upload unencrypted; that is phase G4b and will use this same server mode. Pass 2 was first recorded clean with B5 applied only at the handler; the user asked for a real browser test, which found seven more defects, so pass 2 is rewritten with them and pass 3 is the clean pass.

instruments.evidence: Re-review of G4a-2b after a clean close. The boundary no earlier pass had crossed was the upload itself: the ciphertext the client makes, and what /media/upload does with it.

Read d2697f1f3 (this phase's first review), c421c8a1f, cff7365eb and 04cf8a171. Every one of them tested the upload against a mocked mediaService, so none had ever seen the server's answer to ciphertext.

findings.summary: UploadMedia sniffs an upload's bytes and requires an allowed media type, and ciphertext always sniffs as application/octet-stream, so the server answered every end-to-end encrypted upload with 415. Media sending in messages failed everywhere; it failed closed, so nothing leaked. Every earlier test mocked mediaService, so none had seen the server's answer.

control.observed: With the flag comparison changed so it never matches: four subtests of TestUploadMedia_EncryptedFiles fail, expected 201 actual 415 and expected 413 actual 415, and the serve test fails on the Content-Type of the encrypted file. The package compiles. Without the patch: ok.

findings.summary: mediaService.uploadMedia had no way to say a file was ciphertext, so even a server that could accept encrypted uploads had nothing to act on. The four message media paths now pass { encrypted: true }; other uploads send no flag and are still inspected.

control.observed: With the append removed (tsc still 0): 'tells the server an encrypted file cannot be inspected' fails, AssertionError: expected null to be 'true'. The plain-upload test still passes. Without the patch: 2 passed.

instruments.evidence: Seven source files over two commits. ff2f00f88: UploadMedia gains an encrypted mode, MaxSizeForExtension in security.go, ServeUpload serves an encrypted record as an octet-stream attachment, and media_encrypted_test.go. 9d59cc0dd: mediaService.uploadMedia(file, { encrypted }) and the four message media call sites. Boundaries: the multipart body to /media/upload, the stored media_files row, the served headers, and the stored file_type as later read by SendMessage, the scan worker and the thumbnail queue.
Read d2697f1f3, c421c8a1f, cff7365eb, 04cf8a171 and pass 1 above. The g4a1r2 and g4a2b controls touch files this change edits, so G4 re-applies them.

The artifact the client builds is the FormData handed to api.post. mediaService.upload.test.ts reads it back for two inputs: with { encrypted: true } the body carries encrypted=true and the file; without it the field is absent. The page tests read the same call for three send paths (group composer, direct composer, feed column): all pass { encrypted: true }, with bytes that are not the original.

instruments.why: No component renders anything new. The change adds an argument to four upload calls; the refusal alerts were printed in the first review and did not change.

instruments.evidence: Printed real response bodies from the real handler and a real database for three inputs with a throwaway test (deleted): an encrypted clip.mp4 and notes.pdf return 201 with file_type application/octet-stream and no width, height or thumbnail_url; a plain photo.png returns 201 as image/png with width 4, height 4 and a thumbnail. Refusals were read in media_encrypted_test.go: unmarked ciphertext 415 'Unsupported file type', encrypted .html 415 'Unsupported file extension', limit+17 413 'File size exceeds limit for this file type'.
Read the stored rows back after those uploads: clip.mp4 and notes.pdf are application/octet-stream, scan clean, width NULL; photo.png is image/png with its dimensions. No query or migration changed.

The field name 'encrypted' and its value 'true' are spelled the same in mediaService.ts and in c.PostForm("encrypted") == "true"; the Go test writes the same field. encryptedMediaFileType is the one constant for the stored type on both the upload and the serve side.

Corrected by B5. This row said the bubble decides image or video by message_type. That was wrong: MessageMediaPreview passes message.media_type to FilePreview, which renders by it, so every encrypted image (stored application/octet-stream) was drawn as a download card. The inference helper prefers message_type; the renderer does not. Fixed in 42f1e5a81.

The encrypted rule lives only in UploadMedia. processSingleUpload (batch, used by posts) and the presigned routes keep their own sniffing rules unchanged, and no client sends ciphertext to them: the frontend has no presigned upload call.

Re-applied to the fix. The other ends of the stored octet-stream type: SendMessage requires scan_status clean and copies file_type (fine); the virus scan worker runs validateStagedUpload -- which would refuse octet-stream -- only for pending-uploads/ paths, which /media/upload never writes; thumbnailJobTypeForMIME returns no job for octet-stream; forwarding copies the media fields unchanged.

instruments.why: No struct field was added. The flag is a form field read in one place.

instruments.evidence: The form field is read by c.PostForm, a string accessor. The control patch changes the compared value and the tests fail with 415, so the accessor is exercised, not only declared.

The Go tests post random bytes as the ciphertext. That matches what the client produces for this purpose: pass 1 showed real AES-GCM ciphertext sniffs as application/octet-stream, the same as random bytes, and the handler never decrypts.
Real inputs that must pass: an encrypted .png, .mp4, .pdf and .webm, and one at its class limit plus the 16-byte tag. All 201.

Hostile inputs that must fail: ciphertext without the flag (415); an encrypted .html (415, extension still checked); limit+17 (413). An attacker who marks plaintext HTML as encrypted under a .png name gets it stored as octet-stream and served as an attachment with nosniff, so no browser renders it; TestServeUpload_EncryptedFileIsADownload pins that header pair.

Boundaries: limit+16 accepted, limit+17 refused, both tested. An unknown extension makes MaxSizeForExtension return false and the handler answers 415. The webm case proves the largest class wins for an extension with two classes.

Siblings: batch upload and presigned upload keep full inspection; they carry no message media. The encrypted path keeps every defence it can still use -- extension allow-list, class size cap, quota, virus scan -- and loses only the ones that read content.

With encrypted true, ValidateStrictDocumentStructure still runs but its error is ignored (the condition is '!encrypted && err != nil'); the refusing branch is reachable for plaintext only, as intended. The IsImageType dimension branch is unreachable for encrypted records, as intended.

The client's upload failures reach the user: all four sites alert through messageSendErrorKey with messages.media.uploadFailed as the fallback. The server logs and answers each refusal with its own message.

Searched for conditions on file_type: IsImageType in UploadMedia, thumbnailJobTypeForMIME in the scan worker, the staged-upload check, and ServeUpload. Each treats octet-stream as not-an-image, which is correct for ciphertext.
One constant for the stored type, one helper for the size cap. The three inline copies of the recipient-key lookup are the known E5 item from the first review, unchanged here.

The shape is 'a test mocked the other end, so a contract break was invisible'. Searched every uploadMedia caller: the six non-message callers (group avatar, admin personas, posts, wall, studio) upload plaintext and correctly send no flag. Voice messages still upload unencrypted; that is phase G4b, and it will need the same server mode.

instruments.why: No goroutine or shared state changed.

instruments.evidence: No transaction. A refusal before the file is written leaves nothing; a refusal after it (document structure) removes the file, as before.

instruments.why: No migration.

instruments.evidence: An encrypted record is deleted by the same paths as any media file; nothing type-specific is left behind.

Three controls, each replayed by hand. Server: with the flag comparison changed, TestUploadMedia_EncryptedFiles fails four subtests (expected 201, actual 415; expected 413, actual 415) and TestServeUpload_EncryptedFileIsADownload fails on the Content-Type. Client: without the append, mediaService.upload.test.ts fails 'expected null to be true'. The regenerated feed-column control still fails on the PNG bytes. Every run compiled.
The server guards are reached by the route /media/upload itself; the tests drive the real handler through a gin router.

go build, go vet and gofmt clean; golangci-lint 0 issues on handlers after the stale cache was cleared (see notes); tsc -b 0; eslint 0 on all seven changed frontend files. The pre-commit hook passed both commits.

Six of the seven findings were B5 doing its job: nothing but a real browser against a real stack shows them. The seventh taught a new instrument: the upload gateway discovered CanUserAccessMedia by type assertion, every gateway test built it on models.MediaFileRepository, and main wires repository.PostgresMediaFileRepository, which never delegated it. Added as C8, 'Build it on the implementation production wires'.

Ran it for real: the dev stack (API, worker with ClamAV, Vite) against the dev database and the real bucket, the user signed in the browser pane, and images sent from the composer. The upload itself worked (201, ciphertext in the bucket: 346 bytes for a 330-byte PNG). Everything after it failed, one layer at a time, and each layer is a finding below: the scan job asked the bucket for the wrong key; the composer sent before the scan passed and said nothing; the bubble drew the image as a download card; the browser never sent the session to /uploads/; the server's repository could not authorize anyone; compression broke every streamed file; and the device held a public key that was not its private key's pair. No desk review of the diff could have found any of them.

instruments.why: Nothing starts early.

instruments.evidence: The guards were fed known-bad input: unmarked ciphertext, an .html name, limit+17. Each is refused.

instruments.why: No shared bar or row changed.
No process-wide lazy state is read.

instruments.evidence: The Go tests use database.NewTest against the real test database and ran: 16 handler tests PASS and 17 integration tests PASS, none SKIP. One frontend test skips (MessagesPage.test.tsx:275, keyboard on a checkbox); it is an old it.skip and has nothing to do with media.

The approved plan for G4a-2b was 'seal group media and refuse instead of uploading in the clear'. Media could not be sent at all until this fix, so the fix is what makes the phase keep its promise. The user chose this fix in session.
The upload starts from four entry points, but each call is one user action with its own file; nothing is shared between them.

instruments.why: No overlay changed.

instruments.evidence: Ran every test that imports or mocks a changed module. Frontend: 14 files that name mediaService, MessagesPage, ColumnFeed or ExpandedMessage -- 73 passed, 1 skipped. Go: the middleware package; media_queue_test, uploads_test and media_encrypted_test in handlers (16 tests); and the 17 integration tests that post to /media/upload or send media.

instruments.why: Nothing can cover or redirect the screen.
No shared fixture changed.

instruments.evidence: Re-applied every control whose patch touches a changed file. g4a1r2-edit-box-opened-on-ciphertext still applies. g4a2b-feed-column-uploaded-the-file-itself was stale because this fix added the flag to that call; regenerated with a three-way merge that restores the raw-file upload and keeps the flag, and it still fails both ColumnFeed tests on the PNG bytes.

instruments.why: No resource is acquired after an await in the changed code.
No unmount cleanup changed.
Added to the list at the end of pass 2, from the repository finding; pass 3 applies it.

findings.summary: 356dfd520 moved stored objects under the owner's directory but kept the bare filename as the scan job's s3_key. The worker downloaded a key that does not exist, the scan failed, and the file stayed pending forever, so SendMessage answered 423 for all media wherever object storage and scanning were both on.

control.observed: With the bare filename restored: expected "1/<ts>_note.txt", actual "<ts>_note.txt". Proven first against the real bucket: the owner-directory key exists (346 bytes), the bare key answers 404.

findings.summary: The composer sent the message the moment the upload returned, always before the scan passed, so the server answered 423; the page's onError only spoke for named refusals, so the send failed with no word and the file sat in the composer.

control.observed: With the wait removed: 3 of 4 fail, e.g. 'promise rejected "Error: File is not available until securi..." instead of resolving'. In the browser after the fix the button went Uploading... -> Checking the file... -> Send and the message was sent.

findings.summary: SendMessage copied the stored file_type onto the message, and an encrypted upload is stored as application/octet-stream, so every encrypted photo was drawn as a download card.

control.observed: With the declared type dropped: expected "image/png", actual "application/octet-stream". The refusals (text/html, a type that disagrees with the extension) and the plain-file case still pass, so the control reverts only the fix.

findings.summary: a876d06db scoped the session cookie to /api/, but the app loaded every uploaded file from /uploads/, so no browser sent the session with them; each request was anonymous and every private file answered 404.

control.observed: With the /uploads/ branch restored: expected '/uploads/7/photo.png?v=v2' to be 'http://localhost:8080/api/v1/uploads/...'. The server half (2d871af07) mounts the gateway at /api/v1/uploads/; its test reads, through a cookie jar, what a browser attaches to each route.

findings.summary: The upload gateway asks its repository for CanUserAccessMedia by type assertion; the adapter the server wires never delegated it, so the assertion failed silently and even a file's owner got 404. Every gateway test used the models repository, which has the method.

control.observed: With the delegation removed: the owner case fails, expected 200, actual 404; the stranger and anonymous cases still pass.

findings.summary: The compression middleware gzips any type not on its skip list, including application/octet-stream, while the gateway streams a file from object storage with an exact Content-Length, so the browser dropped the response (ERR_CONTENT_LENGTH_MISMATCH).

control.observed: With the length check removed: 'Should be empty, but was gzip'. A response without its own length is still compressed (a second test).

findings.summary: Old sign-in code published a new public key and then failed, silently, to replace the account's copy, so a copy's private key and the published key can disagree; sign-in, recovery and the scheme move stored the two side by side without comparing them, leaving a device that could open neither its own sender copies nor anything sent to it.

control.observed: With the republish disabled: 3 of the 4 mismatch tests fail. Found in the browser: the device public key equalled the published key, but a round trip public -> private failed with OperationError, and the private key opened only January messages. publicKeyOf is pinned by a real-RSA test.

instruments.evidence: Pass 3 covers the whole review: ff2f00f88..d3d0f9eb4 -- the encrypted upload mode, the upload flag, the scan key, the scan wait and failure messages, the encrypted media type, private files under /api/v1/uploads/, the repository access delegation, the compression length rule, and the key pair rebuild. 27 source and test files.
Read d2697f1f3, c421c8a1f, cff7365eb, 04cf8a171 and passes 1 and 2 of this ledger. No earlier ledger records the cookie path, the adapter delegation or the key pair; each is new.

Printed the artifacts that leave the device: the upload FormData (encrypted=true for message media only), the send request (the same body on every retry, at most ten), and the republish body ({public_key, login_key} after sign-in; {public_key} alone after a no-password recovery). All read in the tests from the mocked API client's received arguments.

The page's changed markup is the Send button label; printed in the real browser with a MutationObserver: Send -> Uploading... -> Send -> Checking the file... -> Send. Images: the January screenshots render as decrypted blobs (2880x1800).

Printed real responses in the browser: GET /api/v1/uploads/7/<file> now 200, application/octet-stream, 629 bytes, where it was 404 (empty body) at /uploads/ and then at /api/v1/uploads/ before the adapter fix, and 200 with ERR_CONTENT_LENGTH_MISMATCH before the compression fix. POST /messages: 423, 423, 201.

Read the stored rows: the encrypted message carries media_type image/png and message_type image; the media row stays application/octet-stream and scan clean. User 7 reads scheme 2, a password copy and a recovery copy (hashes only).

One constant per seam: encryptedMediaFileType on upload, serve and send; the form field 'encrypted'; the cookie path '/api/' against the route prefix '/api/v1/uploads/' (read through a cookie jar); the JSON field public_key on the republish.

The renderer's field is media_type (the pass 2 correction); the server now sets it for encrypted media from the sender's declared type, the field every reader already reads. The upload response's storage_url is what the app resolves through resolveMediaUrl.

Two copies of the uploads URL rule existed (resolveMediaUrl and absoluteMediaUrl in useDecryptedMedia); absoluteMediaUrl is deleted and the hook uses the shared helper. The batch upload and presigned routes keep their own sniffing, and no client sends ciphertext to them.

The other ends, all run: the scan worker downloads the stored key and passes the file; SendMessage accepts after the scan; the gateway serves through the adapter; compression leaves the stream alone; the CSP allows the API origin for images (img-src 'self' data: blob: https:).

instruments.why: No struct field crosses a boundary new; storeNonExtractablePrivateKey now returns {publicKey, matchesPublished}, and every caller consumes both.

instruments.evidence: The type-asserted capability is the accessor: C8's compile-time assertion now fails the build if the adapter loses CanUserAccessMedia again.
The gateway test's fixture is the adapter main wires, not a stand-in; the cookie test uses the real cookie writer; the key test uses real RSA keys.
Real inputs pass: png, mp4, pdf, webm encrypted; an image sent from the real composer; uploads paths with and without a leading slash.

Hostile inputs fail: a declared text/html or a type that disagrees with the extension is refused (400); a stranger and an anonymous request still get 404 through the adapter; a 429 is not retried; a republish never happens when the key matches.
Boundaries: the wait gives up at 30 s with at most ten requests (60 a minute is the send limit); limit+16 accepted, limit+17 refused; a missing declared type keeps the opaque type.

Siblings: ColumnFeed and ExpandedMessage call messagesService.sendMessage and get the scan wait with no change of their own; ColumnFeed already maps errors through messageSendErrorKey, so a timeout reads 'still being checked'. ExpandedMessage still shows its generic send failure; not wrong, less specific.
Every branch reachable: republishIfItDiffers returns early only when the keys match; the wait loop exits on success, on a non-423, or at the deadline.

Failures now reach the person: a failed send alerts (it was silent, including thread replies through ThreadView); a failed republish is logged and retried at the next sign-in, the device staying correct.
Conditions on file_type re-read (scan worker, thumbnails, IsImageType); the only reader that needed the real type was the renderer, fixed via media_type.
Removed the duplicate uploads URL helper (C3). One key-pair rebuild, used by all three copy-opening flows.

Searched for the shape of each finding. The bare-filename key: only the one enqueue; the presigned paths already passed the full key. Optional capability by type assertion: only the gateway's two. A pair stored without comparison: only storeNonExtractablePrivateKey; saveKeys stores a generated pair.

instruments.why: No goroutine or shared state changed.

instruments.evidence: A republish that fails leaves the device correct and the server as it was; the next sign-in retries. A send that times out leaves the upload stored and scanned, unattached.

instruments.why: No migration.

instruments.evidence: An upload that is never sent (a timed-out wait) stays an unattached media row, as any abandoned upload does; nothing new is orphaned.

Seven new controls, each replayed by hand with a real assertion failure and a compiling package: scan-key-missing-owner-directory, send-before-scan-refused, encrypted-media-drawn-as-download, uploads-outside-cookie-path, server-repository-cannot-authorize, gzip-under-exact-length, key-pair-not-rebuilt-from-private-key.
The new guards run on every request through the real route (the gateway, compression) or inside every sign-in (the key rebuild).

go build, go vet, gofmt clean; golangci-lint 0 issues on handlers, middleware, repository and cmd/server; tsc -b 0; eslint and prettier clean on every changed frontend file; the pre-commit hook passed every commit.
Found by B6, which is named; no new instrument. The overflow predates this review, but this review made the button longer, so it is fixed here.

Ran for real again after every fix, against the dev stack and the real bucket, signed in as the user: uploads accepted, the scan passes under the stored key, the composer waits and sends, the January media decrypt and render. Not observed: the key repair itself, which runs only inside a sign-in (only the password opens the copy); the pane still holds the broken pair until the user's next sign-in there. Its logic is pinned by the key-flow tests and a real-RSA test of publicKeyOf.

instruments.why: Nothing starts early: the send waits for the scan rather than racing it.

instruments.evidence: Fed the known-bad input: the orphaned public key (republished), an unexpected declared type (refused), an exact-length octet-stream response (left alone).

Measured the real composer row in the browser at 320 and 375 pixels, with each label the button can show. Before: at 375 even 'Send' ended 35 px past the form edge (clipped on screen), 'Uploading...' 83 px, 'Checking the file...' 65 px and wrapped to two lines; at 320 the button was entirely off the form. The text box kept its intrinsic width. Finding below.

instruments.why: No lazy process-wide state changed.

instruments.evidence: Go ran against the real test database: handlers 759 PASS, 2 SKIP (audio encoder, one a fixed t.Skip, unrelated); middleware and repository ok; 28 integration tests PASS, none skipped. Frontend: 297 passed, 1 skipped (the old MessagesPage keyboard it.skip).

The phase's promise was sealed media that actually works. It now uploads, scans, sends, stores its real type, loads, and decrypts, verified in a real browser; the repair of a mismatched key pair was the user's choice (repair and republish).
A double-clicked Send is already guarded by the disabled button while pending or uploading; the wait keeps it pending.

instruments.why: No overlay or modal changed.

instruments.evidence: Every test that imports or mocks a changed module: 36 frontend files (297 tests); the full handlers, middleware and repository Go packages; the integration tests for media upload, send, forward, thumbnails, group keys and auth. Go was run only after a Codex -race suite in another worktree finished; three narrow control runs had overlapped it before that, and the user was told.

findings.summary: At phone widths the composer's text box kept its intrinsic width and pushed the Send button past the screen edge; the new 'Uploading...' and 'Checking the file...' labels pushed it further.

After the fix, measured in the browser: at 375 and at 320 every label ends at the form edge on one line, the page does not scroll sideways; the label is now 'Checking...', which fits at 320.

instruments.evidence: Whole review again, now to 587693fe2: pass 3's scope plus the composer row fix (two class changes and a shorter label). No backend file changed since the Go runs (git diff d3d0f9eb4..HEAD -- backend is empty).
Read d2697f1f3, c421c8a1f, cff7365eb, 04cf8a171 and passes 1 and 2 of this ledger. No earlier ledger records the cookie path, the adapter delegation or the key pair; each is new.

Printed the artifacts that leave the device: the upload FormData (encrypted=true for message media only), the send request (the same body on every retry, at most ten), and the republish body ({public_key, login_key} after sign-in; {public_key} alone after a no-password recovery). All read in the tests from the mocked API client's received arguments.

The composer row, measured in the browser after the fix: at 375 and 320 px, 'Send', 'Uploading...' and 'Checking...' each end at the form edge on one line; the text box shrinks (78, 30 and 35 px at 320). Label sequence in the real send: Send -> Uploading... -> Send -> Checking... -> Send.

Printed real responses in the browser: GET /api/v1/uploads/7/<file> now 200, application/octet-stream, 629 bytes, where it was 404 (empty body) at /uploads/ and then at /api/v1/uploads/ before the adapter fix, and 200 with ERR_CONTENT_LENGTH_MISMATCH before the compression fix. POST /messages: 423, 423, 201.

Read the stored rows: the encrypted message carries media_type image/png and message_type image; the media row stays application/octet-stream and scan clean. User 7 reads scheme 2, a password copy and a recovery copy (hashes only).

One constant per seam: encryptedMediaFileType on upload, serve and send; the form field 'encrypted'; the cookie path '/api/' against the route prefix '/api/v1/uploads/' (read through a cookie jar); the JSON field public_key on the republish.

The renderer's field is media_type (the pass 2 correction); the server now sets it for encrypted media from the sender's declared type, the field every reader already reads. The upload response's storage_url is what the app resolves through resolveMediaUrl.

Two copies of the uploads URL rule existed (resolveMediaUrl and absoluteMediaUrl in useDecryptedMedia); absoluteMediaUrl is deleted and the hook uses the shared helper. The batch upload and presigned routes keep their own sniffing, and no client sends ciphertext to them.

The other ends, all run: the scan worker downloads the stored key and passes the file; SendMessage accepts after the scan; the gateway serves through the adapter; compression leaves the stream alone; the CSP allows the API origin for images (img-src 'self' data: blob: https:).

instruments.why: No struct field crosses a boundary new; storeNonExtractablePrivateKey now returns {publicKey, matchesPublished}, and every caller consumes both.

instruments.evidence: The type-asserted capability is the accessor: C8's compile-time assertion now fails the build if the adapter loses CanUserAccessMedia again.
The gateway test's fixture is the adapter main wires, not a stand-in; the cookie test uses the real cookie writer; the key test uses real RSA keys.
Real inputs pass: png, mp4, pdf, webm encrypted; an image sent from the real composer; uploads paths with and without a leading slash.

Hostile inputs fail: a declared text/html or a type that disagrees with the extension is refused (400); a stranger and an anonymous request still get 404 through the adapter; a 429 is not retried; a republish never happens when the key matches.
Boundaries: the wait gives up at 30 s with at most ten requests (60 a minute is the send limit); limit+16 accepted, limit+17 refused; a missing declared type keeps the opaque type.

Siblings: ColumnFeed and ExpandedMessage call messagesService.sendMessage and get the scan wait with no change of their own; ColumnFeed already maps errors through messageSendErrorKey, so a timeout reads 'still being checked'. ExpandedMessage still shows its generic send failure; not wrong, less specific.
Every branch reachable: republishIfItDiffers returns early only when the keys match; the wait loop exits on success, on a non-423, or at the deadline.

Failures now reach the person: a failed send alerts (it was silent, including thread replies through ThreadView); a failed republish is logged and retried at the next sign-in, the device staying correct.
Conditions on file_type re-read (scan worker, thumbnails, IsImageType); the only reader that needed the real type was the renderer, fixed via media_type.
Removed the duplicate uploads URL helper (C3). One key-pair rebuild, used by all three copy-opening flows.

Searched for the shape of each finding. The bare-filename key: only the one enqueue; the presigned paths already passed the full key. Optional capability by type assertion: only the gateway's two. A pair stored without comparison: only storeNonExtractablePrivateKey; saveKeys stores a generated pair.
